newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen supported despite low volumes.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen supported despite low volumes.

text.p: German shares were seen well-supported close to their new record highs but traders continued to bemoan the lack of volumes, citing uncertainty ahead of next week's Federal Reserve meeting.
The DAX IBIS index of all-day electronic trade stood 15.38 points higher at 2,640.84, supported by a steady dollar and German Bund market.

Dealers said the expiry of September DAX futures had freed up funds for the cash market but said new client money was limited. "People are asking why they should buy the market now at all at record levels," one said.
Traders said volumes were likely to remain limited until at least after the outcome of the September 24 U.S. Federal Reserve meeting to consider U.S. interest rates.
Export-led stocks, particularly in the chemical sector, performed strongly on the back of the dollar.

Diversified industrial Viag rose 8.30 marks to 582.50 on comments from its management board chairman Georg Obermeier that he expected 1996 operating profit to be a "little better" than 1996 and maintained an open view on the possiblity of a full-year dividend increase.
